key_insight: First-principles calculations identify a class of 109° domain walls in R3c NaNbO₃ with a notably low energy of 9 mJ m⁻².
engineering_relevance: These low-energy walls may help explain crystal twinning and structural phase transitions in NaNbO₃, rather than directly inform solar-cell performance.
method: Classify eight unique domain-wall classes using group theory.
Perform first-principles structural relaxations for representative walls.
evidence_signal: The calculated 109° wall energy is comparable to low-energy ferroelectric walls in BaTiO₃, and this wall class is compatible with experimentally observed twinning.
watch_item: The abstract proposes an atomistic R3c ↔ Pbcm transition mechanism but reports neither direct experimental validation nor AI or photovoltaic evaluation.
